title: Preflight runbook checks and escalation lane — 2026-05-18
content:
Purpose: quick pre-shift checklist + active escalation lane for the morning watch. Use this to triage fast, hand off clearly, and note any runbook gaps to fix after shift.

Meta
- Shift owner: Ethan Morales (morning watch)
- Coverage: 06:30-14:30 PT
- Handoff to: Priya K. (afternoon) at 14:15 PT in #sre-ops
- Primary channels: #sre-ops, #prod-incidents, PagerDuty (SRE-morning)

Immediate items (preflight)
1) Alert queue sanity check (06:35)
   - Run: check-alerts.sh (quick filter for >5% error rate across endpoints)
   - Known chaff: heartbeat timeouts from datadog-agent on -staging (suppress filter applied)
2) Model serving health (06:45)
   - Console: check per-model latency panels (p95) for top 10 routes
   - Look for sudden KV cache-miss surges on kv-cache-prod (typical early-morning cold start)
3) Dedicated pools & autoscale (07:00)
   - Validate Dedicated GPU pool capacity: reserved-util < 85% and autoscale enabled for burst
   - If reserved-util >90% -> open INC and trigger immediate scale policy (see escalation lane)

Active escalations / follow-ups (as of 07:25)
- INC-4821: sporadic 429s on embeddings endpoint for customer-acct "acme-x"
  - Triage notes: throttles appear correlated with a single client key hitting 3x usual QPS for 512-length embeddings. Rate limit token-bucket drained then recovered.
  - Action taken: temporarily throttle key at API gateway (done), created ephemeral bump in Dedicated pool for embeddings-heavy backend (requested).
  - Follow-ups: update rate-limit runbook to include binary search steps for client keys and example gd-priority rules. Owner: Priya (due 2026-05-20).

Runbook gaps noticed (to annotate)
- "model-fallback-policy.md" missing decision tree for cross-region fallback when model variant A is overloaded but variant B has longer latency; add guidance on user-visible latency SLO vs. cost.
- Embeddings throttling playbook: needs explicit commands for forcing soft-throttle vs hard-throttle in API GW (examples below).

Quick commands (copy/paste)
- Check recent 429s: $ curl -s "https://console.redwood.ai/api/alerts?query=429&since=15m" | jq .hits
- Inspect KV cache metrics: $ kcachectl --env prod stat --last 30m | grep miss_rate
- Temporary throttle a key (api-gw): $ api-gw throttle add --key <KEY> --rate 10/s --duration 30m

Priority lane (what to escalate now)
- P0: service-wide degradation (model-serving p95 > 2s across >30% pods)
- P1: customer-impacting throttles (single-customer causing >20% error spike)
- P2: isolated pod crashes / OOMs with restart loop

Notes to incoming shift (Priya)
- Confirm INC-4821 mitigation holds after 30m. If 429s persist, escalate to platform-eng and open an emergency scaling rollback for last deploy (see linked PR).
- Keep an eye on latency heatmap for chat routes — we saw a 10% tail increase after the 03:00 deploy; likely related to KV cache TTL misalignment.
- If autoscaler shows heavy tail scaling delays (>90s to add pods), route to infra-oncall and paste the autoscaler logs snippet: `controller: scale-delay`

Post-shift follow-ups (todo list)
- Ethan: 1) Draft runbook section for embeddings rate limiting (due 2026-05-20). 2) Add RV tests for cross-region fallback.
- Priya: 1) Validate Dedicated pool scaling logs and attach to INC-4821. 2) Verify customer communication template used is correct.
- Marisol: run through runbook friction points in next runbook refactor session (2026-05-21).

Open questions (for runbook review)
- What should the immediate fallback priority be when both model variants are available but have differing cost/latency? Add decision matrix.
- Should we automate soft-throttle suggestion in Console when a key jumps >2x baseline?

Short postmortem notes (if INC-4821 becomes P1->P0)
- Timeline capture: exact time throttle applied, when autoscale request completed, when 429s dropped below baseline. Save request traces and correlate with API gateway logs.

End-of-shift handoff checklist (to tick)
- [ ] Confirm alerts filtered/acknowledged
- [ ] Confirm all active escalations have clear owners + ETA
- [ ] Upload any new logs to INC ticket and link to Confluence
- [ ] Mark runbook items with GitHub issue if edits required

If anything spikes while I'm on-call ping me directly (sms) or flag @Ethan in #prod-incidents.

-- Ethan M.

(Notes: this is a working doc; edit in place rather than creating clones. If you take ownership of a follow-up, add your name under the action.)
